headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because TREK handles secrets and networked collaboration while pdf.js can ingest PDF content that may be treated as trusted input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and runs in a browser-based test model, while TREK is a real-time collaborative app with MCP and browser access. A PDF can carry attacker-controlled content that TREK may later consume through shared workflows or copied output. The pairwise bridge is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK imports or displays text extracted from pdf.js output without sanitization
IF a PDF from pdf.js is copied into TREK via MCP or browser workflow
mitigations: Sanitize extracted PDF text before TREK consumes it
Disable MCP paths that accept raw document text
Add a provenance label to pdf.js-derived content
Review one sample PDF-to-TREK workflow for instruction-like text

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and logs them in a self-hosted collaborative environment with allowlisted egress. pdf.js processes PDF documents and can expose their contents to the surrounding browser context. If sensitive PDFs are opened or transferred between them, TREK's broader data classes make leakage materially worse.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are opened in pdf.js and then copied into TREK
IF TREK stores or forwards document contents containing secrets or personal data
mitigations: Restrict TREK uploads to non-sensitive documents
Separate pdf.js and TREK workspaces
Turn off logging for document payloads in TREK
Scan uploaded PDFs for secrets before import
Use a redaction step before any transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both write to files, but their writable surfaces differ: pdf.js handles PDF files, while TREK writes travel.db, uploads, and logs. There is no direct evidence of shared locking or a shared directory, so conflict is plausible but not proven at high severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem path
IF TREK and pdf.js modify the same document set without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Use file locks for shared documents
Avoid concurrent edits to the same PDF or database
Mount TREK storage read-only for pdf.js

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in and MCP, so it may treat upstream content as actionable. pdf.js renders PDF content that can be mistaken for authoritative text. Without a documented verification step between them, A's output can cascade into B's planning or messaging workflows.
conditions: IF TREK uses pdf.js output as source material for plans or reservations
IF no human verification step is inserted before TREK acts on extracted text
mitigations: Require human review before TREK acts on PDF-derived facts
Mark pdf.js output as untrusted in TREK
Add citation checks for extracted claims
Block automatic booking from document text

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles country visit history, user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while pdf.js processes PDF documents. If those PDFs contain regulated personal data, TREK's broader retention and logging surfaces create a compliance mismatch risk. pdf.js is open-source and local, so it is not the main residency concern.
conditions: IF PDFs contain personal data or travel records
IF TREK logs or retains imported document contents longer than intended
mitigations: Classify uploaded PDFs before import
Set a short retention window for TREK logs
Delete imported documents after processing
Document residency and retention for travel data
Redact identifiers before storage
